plan: Given my value of $23, I will aim to win the auction by bidding slightly above a midpoint value while ensuring profit. Bidding my full value is dominated, as I risk paying more than I gain. I will bid $15 to balance winning chances and potential profit, assuming others bid around the average value ($24.5). This bid could win if others undervalue their bids, and it ensures profit if I pay a third-highest bid lower than $23.

Since this is a single round, my aim is to maximize profit immediately. My value is $18, so I should bid below this to ensure profit if I win. Bidding exactly $18 risks no profit. Dominated bids include those above $18. To avoid overbidding, I'll consider bids like $10-$15, balancing between winning chances and profit. A bid of $12 offers a good chance to win without overpaying.

With a private value of $39, I aim to bid slightly above the average to maximize profit while avoiding overbidding. Dominated bids are those above $39 since winning would incur losses. I should bid close to my value to outbid others but still ensure a positive profit. A bid of $38.5 is strategic: it challenges competitors without exceeding my value, ensuring that if I win, my profit margin remains positive.
